hints: A yes/no comparison divides the remaining integer range.
Ask whether the midpoint is less than the hidden number.
Maintain inclusive lower and upper bounds until they coincide.
analogy: Each answer discards roughly half of the possible numbers.
example: For x=7 in range [1,10], asking y=5 gives YES, then y=8 gives NO, narrowing the range to [6,8].
algorithm: Set low=1 and high=10^9. While low<high, query y=floor((low+high)/2), flush, and read the reply. On YES set low=y+1; otherwise set high=y. Print ! followed by low, flush, and terminate.
correctness: The response tells exactly whether x lies above y or at most y. Each update keeps x in the remaining interval, which shrinks to one value.
complexity: The range contains 10^9 values, so at most 30 queries and O(1) extra space are needed.
